 GITSN Deploys Security Equipment for Public Verification of Perfect LEET Scorer
 Alpha-W and Alpha-P to monitor wireless signals during Lee Jin-woo’s live Korean exam
 sung ji on 
 Published 2026.11.19 14:03
 Reply 0
 Character Size Settings

 이 기사를 공유합니다 
 Lee Jin-woo, who achieved a perfect score on the LEET. (Photo: Lee Jin-woo’s social media) 
 Wireless security company GITSN will deploy radio-frequency detection equipment at a public examination scheduled for November 19, where Lee Jin-woo, who achieved a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), plans to demonstrate his ability by solving Korean-language questions from the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute, which is organizing the broadcast, reportedly made an urgent request to GITSN the previous day to install the equipment.
 GITSN said on November 18 that it would provide its Alpha-W private wireless security system and Alpha-P portable radio-frequency detector for the public examination organized by IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute.
 The two devices do not incorporate GITSN’s AI-based cheating detection software, which has completed development and is scheduled for release by the end of this year. However, GITSN said the existing equipment can detect wireless signals, including Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
 “To transmit exam questions captured with smart glasses or miniature cameras to an external AI system and receive answers, devices must generate Bluetooth signals for device-to-device connections or Wi-Fi and mobile communication signals for external access,” a GITSN official said. “Our equipment detects these signals as soon as they occur, allowing supervisors to immediately identify unauthorized devices at the examination site.”
 The official added that GITSN employees were currently installing the equipment at the venue.
 Alpha-W and Alpha-P scan frequencies ranging from 25 kilohertz (kHz) to 8 gigahertz (GHz) at intervals of approximately one second.
 The equipment is being provided following a request from IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute the previous day. THE ELEC contacted the institute to ask why it had decided to introduce the equipment just two days before the examination but received no response.
 Lee has faced allegations of cheating using AI devices. He has denied the allegations and announced plans to demonstrate his abilities by taking the CSAT Korean-language examination on the day of the actual test. IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute was selected as the independent organizer through a public recruitment process initiated by Lee to address the allegations.
 The examination will be broadcast live in a single continuous take on IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute’s YouTube channel starting at 8 a.m. on November 19. Lee is scheduled to answer 56 CSAT Korean-language questions within 65 minutes.
 In a notice posted on its website, IDA Entrance Exam Research Institute said participants would be required to surrender all personal electronic devices and belongings, change into designated clothing, and undergo metal detector and radio-frequency detector screening to ensure fairness. An ear endoscopy examination will also be conducted in the presence of a medical professional.
 “This public verification is not intended to defend or criticize any particular individual,” the institute said. “At a time of heightened public interest in examination fairness, we aim to demonstrate what procedures and records can enable objective public verification.” However, the institute also added that it had been unable to contact Lee.
